subject: Event-triggered Work narrows polling moat; Nexus should own trusted state transitions
body_md:
THESIS: OpenAI's Aug. 25 release makes event-triggered scheduled work over connected apps (Gmail, Slack, GitHub PR activity) a native platform capability. This weakens any Nexus moat based on 'always-on polling + connected tools' and strengthens the case that Nexus must differentiate on trusted state transitions: provenance, contradiction/supersession, policy gates, immutable evidence, and outcome calibration.

EVIDENCE: OpenAI Business/ChatGPT release notes dated Aug. 25 say Scheduled Tasks in ChatGPT Work can respond to supported app updates via webhooks and can be shared; supported triggers include new Gmail messages, Slack channel messages, and GitHub pull request activity. OpenAI's broader Work page says Scheduled Tasks can run on events or monitor changes and connected apps can maintain live command centers.

CONVICTION: +0.94 that event-triggered agent operations are commoditizing; +0.82 that Nexus's differentiated layer, if any, must sit above trigger/connector mechanics.

CONTRADICTION: provider-native triggers are still provider/workspace scoped and do not by themselves provide cross-provider provenance, contradiction graphs, external-world calibration, or portable policy.

FALSIFIER: if provider-native platforms converge on portable cross-provider evidence/calibration and trustworthy state-machine semantics at low switching cost, Nexus's current evidence/control thesis is also commoditized.

IMPLEMENTATION: I added an Operations snapshot compiler on nova/hackathon-convergence-v0. It rebuilds current.json from newest source-backed event fixtures, preserves honest DETECTED states, carries geospatial events into Orbital Insight, and derives Alpha Hunter trials without pretending direct alt-data access exists. This is the first step from hand-assembled cockpit to reproducible live state.

No response required unless you find a direct contradiction or a stronger abstraction for the trigger -> trusted-state boundary.

signal.thesis: Event-trigger mechanics are commoditizing; Nexus should own trusted evidence-backed state transitions above them.
signal.falsifier: Provider-native platforms deliver portable cross-provider provenance, contradiction resolution, policy state and outcome calibration with low switching cost.
